review_scope: AICP protocol repository at the M67 security-coverage boundary

threats.title: Canonicalization edge cases
threats.description: Different JSON spellings, Unicode ordering, or canonical byte construction could produce inconsistent hashes or signatures.
threats.residual_boundary: The evidence covers AICP's registered JCS/hash domains; it does not attest arbitrary non-AICP serialization code.

threats.title: Hash-chain and replay manipulation
threats.description: Messages could be replayed, duplicated, or detached from their declared predecessor chain.
threats.residual_boundary: The checks reject transcript-local replay and chain inconsistency; durable storage and cross-deployment replay windows remain deployment concerns.

threats.title: Required signed-flow truncation
threats.description: A required mediated signed security flow could be presented only as a valid signed prefix.
threats.residual_boundary: Only truncation of this suite-declared required security flow is rejected; a generic valid transcript prefix is not made invalid.

threats.title: Core v0.2 contract, proposal, and active-head substitution
threats.description: An acceptance or subsequent action could be rebound to a stale, future, cross-contract, or substituted proposal, contract, context, conflict candidate, or active head.
threats.residual_boundary: The corpus proves deterministic exact-agreement state transitions, not endpoint honesty or local-policy correctness.

threats.title: Signature and signed-path integrity
threats.description: A signed security-path message could carry a stale object hash, invalid signature, or signer mismatch.
threats.residual_boundary: This covers paths that select signed-message requirements; it does not make signatures mandatory for every extension message.

threats.title: Enforcement sender spoofing
threats.description: A sender outside the contract's ext.enforcement.enforcers set could issue a verdict.
threats.residual_boundary: Authorization is checked against the negotiated contract; cryptographic sender authentication is separately profile-dependent.

threats.title: Enforcement gate, target, and verdict-reference substitution
threats.description: Delivery could follow DENY, bind ALLOW to a different target hash, or cite an unresolved verdict message.
threats.residual_boundary: The check enforces exact blocking-mode bindings and does not introduce a universal verdict-signature MUST.

threats.title: Alert registry and action integrity
threats.description: An ALERT could use an unregistered code or recommended action while appearing protocol-valid.
threats.residual_boundary: Registry integrity does not authenticate the sender; EXT-ALERTS permits any sender to emit ALERT.

threats.title: Generic EXT-ALERTS sender authenticity
threats.description: A receiver may want proof that a generic ALERT came from an authorized or authenticated alerting principal.
threats.residual_boundary: Generic EXT-ALERTS has no universal authorized-sender set; deployments or selected authenticated profiles must supply that policy.
threats.defer_reason: Current EXT-ALERTS explicitly permits any sender to emit ALERT, so a universal sender-authentication rejection rule would strengthen the protocol incompatibly.

threats.title: Signed ALERT authenticity on selected signed paths
threats.description: An ALERT on a suite-selected signed security path could be modified or signed with invalid key material.
threats.residual_boundary: Authenticity is established only where the selected security path actually requires and verifies signatures.

threats.title: CAPNEG v0.1 downgrade and stale-declaration rollback
threats.description: A proposal could select a profile outside a participant's most recent exact declaration or unilaterally downgrade an accepted result.
threats.residual_boundary: The check uses exact latest-declaration semantics and does not rank profiles by an invented implementation-independent security strength.

threats.title: CAPNEG v0.2 composition downgrade and substitution
threats.description: A composed profile set could be omitted, injected, mixed across Core families, rolled back, partially accepted, or rebound to substituted hashes, contracts, declarations, or projections.
threats.residual_boundary: Declaration authority, participant truthfulness, off-transcript consensus, transport security, and external organizational trust remain outside exact transcript composition checks.

threats.title: OBJECT_RESYNC integrity and explicit security-status mechanisms
threats.description: A FOUND response could misbind object type/content/hash, while ACCESS_DENIED, TOO_LARGE, and REDACTED mechanisms could lack interoperable coverage.
threats.residual_boundary: The suite proves exact mechanisms and FOUND integrity, not that one response status or numeric cap is universally mandatory.

threats.title: OBJECT_RESYNC object-existence concealment
threats.description: NOT_FOUND may disclose whether an object exists when a deployment would prefer ACCESS_DENIED.
threats.residual_boundary: The protocol represents ACCESS_DENIED, but the choice between ACCESS_DENIED and NOT_FOUND remains the responder's selected local policy.
threats.defer_reason: EXT-OBJECT-RESYNC permits ACCESS_DENIED instead of NOT_FOUND based on policy; making concealment universal would reject currently conformant implementations.

threats.title: OBJECT_RESYNC amplification and resource exhaustion
threats.description: Object retrieval can consume bandwidth, storage, CPU, or request capacity at deployment scale.
threats.residual_boundary: Deployments must select authentication, quotas, byte budgets, concurrency limits, and rate controls appropriate to their threat environment.
threats.defer_reason: The RFC's DoS/amplification mitigation is SHOULD-level guidance and defines no universal rate or byte limit that M67 can enforce compatibly.

threats.title: RESUME probing and forced resynchronization loops
threats.description: Repeated UNKNOWN_SESSION probes or NEEDS_RESYNC responses could enumerate sessions or force non-progress loops.
threats.residual_boundary: The deterministic abuse patterns are detected; deployment-scale throttling remains a local control.

threats.title: Operational ALERT verbosity
threats.description: Human-readable ALERT content could exceed the repository's explicit minimization and safe-lint bounds.
threats.residual_boundary: The check enforces known length/verbosity mechanics and is not a universal semantic secret classifier.

threats.title: Arbitrary semantic secret classification
threats.description: Human-readable ALERT, evidence, or application text may contain domain-specific secrets not identifiable from syntax alone.
threats.residual_boundary: A deployment must select a data-classification and redaction policy for its own business data and secret types.
threats.defer_reason: AICP 0.1 defines no universal taxonomy that can decide whether arbitrary application text is a secret; a global regex would create false protocol claims.

threats.title: Harness-created bearer and TLS secret leakage
threats.description: Known Authorization values, generated bearer controls, TLS private keys, or child environment secrets could enter serialized live-evidence reports.
threats.residual_boundary: The harness can prove absence of secrets it creates and controls; it does not classify arbitrary user payload data.

threats.title: Public evidence schema test-control fields
threats.description: Evidence and Pairwise schemas could accidentally require or expose HTTP credentials, private TLS keys, or full process environments.
threats.residual_boundary: The structural audit excludes known harness-control fields and does not scan or reject arbitrary application payload text.

threats.title: Mediator delivery after DENY
threats.description: A blocking mediator could deliver content after a valid DENY verdict.
threats.residual_boundary: The transcript proves deterministic gate behavior, not the integrity of a compromised mediator host.

threats.title: Live-binding control and transport abuse
threats.description: Live HTTP/MCP evidence could be forged through non-loopback targets, redirects, shell/environment injection, unbounded subprocess IO, bearer reflection, TLS-key leakage, fake certificate rejection, session/cursor confusion, or JSON-RPC/build substitution.
threats.residual_boundary: Production TLS configuration, IAM, public reachability, DDoS resistance, and organizational identity remain deployment or external-trust concerns.

threats.title: Generalized-evidence report, mark, target, and release forgery
threats.description: A report could claim an unearned compatibility mark, substitute a target or release, or present stale provenance as current.
threats.residual_boundary: The evidence proves consistency and reproducibility of exact artifacts; it is not remote attestation or proof of organizational identity.

threats.title: Generalized-evidence artifact multiplicity, answer leakage, and semantic mutation
threats.description: Required artifacts could be missing or duplicated, producer requests could reveal oracle answers, or evaluator semantics could be bypassed by mutation.
threats.residual_boundary: The controls bind the registered TCK execution; they do not prove that a self-declared implementation is operated by an independent organization.

threats.title: Generalized-evidence subject and build substitution
threats.description: Evidence produced by one subject or build could be relabeled as another implementation.
threats.residual_boundary: Exact self-declared subject/build binding is checked; no remote hardware attestation is claimed.

threats.title: Independent organizational identity and remote attestation
threats.description: A repository evidence subject may self-declare build identity without proving independent organizational control or remotely attested hardware state.
threats.residual_boundary: Consumers must establish organizational identity and hardware/runtime trust through external systems when required.
threats.defer_reason: Current AICP evidence binds declared subjects and exact artifacts but defines neither a remote-attestation protocol nor an organizational-independence authority.

threats.title: Pairwise side-report and peer-build substitution
threats.description: Unrelated side reports, contradictory role descriptors, or the same build masquerading as two peers could be combined into a Pairwise claim.
threats.residual_boundary: The exact builds and independently observed roles are bound within the run; repository clean-room peers do not count as external adoption.

threats.title: Pairwise relay and harness injection
threats.description: The harness could author MCP requests or responses, rewrite relay bytes, route to the wrong server, or execute only one side.
threats.residual_boundary: The tests establish repository harness causality for the registered pairwise target, not internet-scale network-path integrity.

threats.title: Pairwise first-seen, replay, and release provenance
threats.description: Peer hashes or challenges could be pre-seeded, a stale/cross-run transcript replayed, final poll omitted, or Pairwise release authority substituted.
threats.residual_boundary: Pairwise TCK 1.3 proves exact registered run causality and provenance; it does not create a real external relationship.

threats.title: Endpoint, key-custody, and host compromise
threats.description: A compromised endpoint, stolen signing key, or hostile host/runtime can act with the authority available to that component.
threats.residual_boundary: Deployments remain responsible for endpoint hardening, runtime isolation, key custody, rotation, and incident response.
threats.defer_reason: Protocol signatures and exact bindings cannot guarantee that endpoints, private keys, or their host runtime are uncompromised.

threats.title: Production DDoS resistance and universal rate limiting
threats.description: Protocol endpoints can be exhausted by transport-scale or application-scale request volume.
threats.residual_boundary: Operators must select network controls, quotas, authentication, autoscaling, circuit breakers, and rate limits for their environment.
threats.defer_reason: AICP defines no universal traffic budget and does not guarantee internet-scale DDoS resistance.

threats.title: Correctness of arbitrary local policy
threats.description: A conformant implementation may select a local authorization, privacy, or enforcement policy that is unsuitable for its deployment.
threats.residual_boundary: Policy owners must validate selected rules, data classifications, authorities, and exception handling against deployment requirements.
threats.defer_reason: Deterministic protocol conformance can validate selected-policy structure and outcomes but cannot decide whether an arbitrary local policy is correct.

threats.title: Confidentiality of arbitrary application payloads
threats.description: Base AICP payloads may contain application data whose confidentiality depends on the selected profile and transport deployment.
threats.residual_boundary: Deployments must select appropriate confidentiality profiles, transport protection, access controls, retention, and redaction policy.
threats.defer_reason: The base protocol does not promise confidentiality for arbitrary application payloads without an appropriate selected profile and deployment controls.

threats.title: Independent external security review
threats.description: Internal tests and review artifacts do not substitute for assessment by an independent external reviewer.
threats.residual_boundary: No completed contracted independent-review artifact exists in the repository.
threats.defer_reason: Independent review requires a real third-party engagement and contract-complete report; M67 and its internal evidence cannot manufacture that external fact.

threats.title: Model truthfulness and semantic correctness
threats.description: An agent or model can produce false, misleading, or semantically incorrect content in a structurally conformant message.
threats.residual_boundary: Applications remain responsible for model evaluation, human oversight, source verification, and domain-specific correctness controls.
threats.defer_reason: AICP validates protocol structure and selected deterministic rules; it cannot universally decide whether arbitrary model output is truthful.

threats.title: CAPNEG declaration authority and truthfulness
threats.description: A participant may make a syntactically valid capability declaration that is unauthorized or untruthful about the implementation behind it.
threats.residual_boundary: Deployments must authenticate principals and decide which declaration authorities and attestations they trust.
threats.defer_reason: CAPNEG deterministically binds the latest declarations and negotiated result but does not define a universal organizational authority for declaration truthfulness.
